basis: Existing Construction.quote at recursive Goods prices; 100 coins per sailor-day. Working fuel, ammunition and supplies are purchased separately.

hulls.basis: Open Reedwater net dory with a hand reel, salvage drum and one light defense gun. Its short planked hull and single propulsion assembly keep the physical building bill small.
hulls.name: Kelpnet Dory

hulls.basis: Compact working launch with a long stern, line davit and paired drums under a customs canopy. Extra planking and bilge equipment support a modest catch hold.
hulls.name: Brinehook Longliner

hulls.basis: Broad estuary catamaran with a cross-beam work deck, twin net reels and covered net stacks. Two propulsion assemblies move the timber-heavy trawling hull; its single light gun is for defense.
hulls.name: Mother Gull Trawler

hulls.basis: Flat estuary lighter carrying lashed bale stacks on both hulls beneath a low span bridge. Cargo framing favors timber and logs over armor; one light gun leaves the other sockets optional.
hulls.name: Fenhopper Lighter

hulls.basis: Long coastal catamaran with a packet prow crest and bonded strongboxes. Hull-area planking and twin propulsion assemblies dominate the yard bill rather than military armor.
hulls.name: Tideledger Coaster

hulls.basis: Civilian packet with a high packet-house bridge, broad cargo framing and covered manifests. More hold space than the Sovereign Armed Packet trades armor and ordnance for planks, pumps and cargo access.
hulls.name: Fourport Packet

hulls.basis: Wide motor-driven cargo galleon with a packet house and cargo derrick masts, without working sails. Three propulsion assemblies and extensive timber framing make the largest civilian building bill; only one light defense gun is installed.
hulls.name: Brasswind Motor-Galleon

hulls.basis: Civilian foundry barge with a low turtleback wheelhouse, manifold banks and secured casks. High pump capacity demands copper, supplies and paid mechanics; the hold uses ordinary finite cargo custody.
hulls.name: Seepoil Tanker Barge

hulls.basis: Long civilian fleet tanker with a practical wheelhouse and manifold runs along both rails. Its heavy pumping fit and three propulsion assemblies need substantial copper, mechanics and engineering supervision, with no automatic fuel delivery.
hulls.name: Blackwater Fleet Tanker

hulls.basis: Motor hydrofoil pleasure launch with a stepped cockpit, trim cells and coiled docking ropes. Its numerical crew are sailors; speed-driven propulsion takes precedence over a tiny cargo hold.
hulls.name: Gullwing Daysailer

hulls.basis: Cabin cruiser with an interceptor canopy, signal tube and fitted lockers. Cabin joinery adds four plank bundles and three repair kits to the derived hull recipe, including their existing paid supply chains and shipwright work.
hulls.name: Lacquered Osprey Cruiser

hulls.basis: High-ranking civilian yacht with a commodore tower, signal wings and household cabins. Eight extra plank bundles and six repair kits fund the fitted interior through existing material and labor bills; household staff count within its numerical crew.
hulls.name: Aurelian Viceroy Yacht
